label: Bible Study
prompt: And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said, Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be _____; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.
verse: And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said, Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.
note: Moses' marching prayer whenever the ark set out — David echoes it at the start of Psalm 68.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be _____ thee.
verse: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.
note: Friends carried a paralyzed man to Jesus on a bed, and the first thing He gave him was forgiveness.

label: Sunday School
prompt: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing _____ he went.
verse: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
note: Abraham obeyed and left home 'not knowing whither he went' — the first great road trip without a map.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in _____ to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
verse: Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
note: Samuel, rejected as judge when Israel demanded a king, still counts it a sin to stop praying for them.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, _____ thou what thou readest?
verse: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
note: Philip runs alongside the Ethiopian's chariot and opens with the best question in evangelism history.
